- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for the next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 2–5% in the following 2–4 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and prices are trending upward, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for the next 3–5 days.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price decline, forecast should not drop below 1–2% below recent low; cap downward correction.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate in high-sentiment periods; add 1–3% to forecast if sentiment >0.6 over last 7 days.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 3 days, model often lags; adjust forecast upward by 1–4% in the 2nd–3rd day of sentiment shift.
